Consumer complaint narrative: Our loan documents contain provisions stating that the lender 's prior written consent is required before transferring all or any part of the property or any interest in the property. Specifically : Note dated XX/XX/XXXX, Page XXXX, third paragraph ; and Note dated XX/XX/XXXX, Page XXXX, first paragraph. Both notes provide, in relevant part : " If all or any part of the Property or any interest in the Property is sold or transferred [ ... ] without Lender XXXX prior written consent, Lender may require immediate payment in full of all sums secured by this instrument. '' Because these provisions expressly refer to the lender 's prior written consent, we have sought written confirmation from Truist Bank before recording any deed transferring title to our revocable living trust. Over the course of our communications, Truist first requested a Certification of XXXX. We provided the requested document. Truist subsequently requested an affidavit, which we also provided. After satisfying those requests, Truist then requested a recorded copy of the title transfer. This places us in an impossible position. We can not safely record and transfer title first because the loan documents state that a transfer without the lender 's prior written consent may permit the lender to accelerate the loan and demand immediate payment in full. Accordingly, we have repeatedly requested written confirmation from Truist before proceeding with the transfer. We have written to Truist on at least XXXX separate occasions ( XX/XX/XXXX, XX/XX/XXXX, XX/XX/XXXX ) explaining the relevant provisions of the loan documents and requesting written confirmation that : The transfer of title into our revocable living trust is permitted ; and The existing loan will remain in full force and effect without acceleration, enforcement of any due-on-sale provision, or modification of its terms. Despite these repeated requests, Truist has not provided a clear written response addressing our concerns. We have already provided Truist with documentation demonstrating that : The trust is a revocable inter vivos trust. Current owners will remain the trustees and beneficiaries of the trust. There is no transfer of rights of occupancy. The property will continue to be occupied by the borrowers as applicable. The transfer does not constitute a sale or conveyance to any third party. The transfer is solely for estate-planning purposes. In addition, we understand that transfers of residential property by a borrower into the borrower 's own revocable living trust, where the borrower remains a beneficiary and occupancy rights remain unchanged, are generally protected under the GarnSt. Germain Depository Institutions Act of XXXX, XXXX U.S.C. XXXX, and its implementing regulations. Our proposed transfer appears to satisfy those conditions. Despite our repeated explanations and submission of the requested trust documentation, Truist has not provided a clear written statement regarding whether it agrees that the proposed transfer qualifies under those protections. Instead, Truist continues to request a recorded deed before providing the written confirmation we have requested. Our concern is straightforward. The loan documents warn that a transfer without prior written consent may permit acceleration of the loan. Truist, however, is effectively requiring us to complete the transfer before providing the written confirmation necessary to protect ourselves from that risk. We have explained this concern multiple times, but Truist has not addressed it. The ongoing delay is preventing us from completing an important estate-planning transfer. We established our revocable living trust to avoid probate and ensure proper management and disposition of our assets. Further delay increases the risk that the property may remain outside the trust and become subject to probate proceedings, contrary to our estate-planning objectives.

Consumer complaint narrative: I am filing this complaint against I.C. System, Inc. regarding a collection account they are furnishing to the nationwide consumer reporting agencies on behalf of XXXX XXXXXXXX XXXX XXXX ( XXXX ) in the approximate amount of {$470.00}. As a result, I was deprived of the opportunity to meaningfully evaluate or challenge the account before it negatively affected my credit profile. Because I dispute the account, I request that I.C. System produce competent evidence demonstrating both the validity of the alleged debt and the accuracy of every item of information it furnished to the consumer reporting agencies. Specifically, I request the following : The complete account history from XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX. The original service agreement or other documentation establishing my legal responsibility for the account. The service address associated with the account. Every monthly billing statement. The final billing statement. A complete payment ledger. A detailed itemization explaining how the alleged balance of {$470.00} was calculated. Documentation showing the date the account was referred or assigned to I.C. System. Documentation establishing I.C. Systems authority to collect on behalf of XXXX XXXXXXXX XXXX XXXX. The date any validation notice was allegedly mailed. The address to which that notice was allegedly mailed. Documentation supporting every item of information reported to XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX I further request that I.C. System explain the procedures it used to determine that the information it furnished to the consumer reporting agencies was complete, accurate, and supported by competent documentation. As a furnisher of information to consumer reporting agencies, I.C. System has obligations under the Fair Credit Reporting Act ( FCRA ) to furnish information with accuracy and integrity. Information that can not be substantiated through a reasonable investigation should not remain on a consumers credit report. Likewise, as a debt collector, I.C. System is expected to comply with the applicable requirements of the Fair Debt Collection Practices Act ( FDCPA ) concerning the collection of consumer debts and communications with consumers. If I.C. System contends that it complied with those obligations, I request that it produce the documentation supporting that position. If I.C. System can not produce competent documentation establishing : that I am legally responsible for the alleged debt, that the balance reported is accurate, that the account was properly reported, that it possessed authority to collect the account, and that its reporting complies with applicable federal law, then I request that this collection account be permanently deleted from XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX Merely stating that the account has been verified is insufficient. I request documentary evidence supporting the verification. I also request that the CFPB require I.C. System to conduct a reasonable investigation and provide copies of every document upon which it relies. Should I.C. System be unable to substantiate the account with competent documentary evidence, continued reporting would be inaccurate and misleading and should cease immediately. Accordingly, I respectfully request the following relief : Conduct a complete investigation into this disputed account. Require I.C. System to produce all documentation supporting the debt. Require I.C. System to explain the basis for furnishing the account to the nationwide consumer reporting agencies. Delete the account from XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX if it can not be fully substantiated. Correct any inaccurate, incomplete, or misleading information. Confirm the results of the investigation in writing. I appreciate the CFPBs assistance in ensuring compliance with federal consumer protection laws and maintaining the accuracy of consumer credit reporting

Consumer complaint narrative: XXXX XXXX XXXX Wells Fargo 's Handling of a XXXX XXXX XXXX and Customer Service Failures Complainant : XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX : Wells Fargo Bank , N.A . Nature of Complaint I am submitting this complaint regarding Wells Fargo 's handling of a XXXX payment that was placed under a security review, the bank 's failure to notify me that my funds had been restricted, repeated refusals to provide access to the department responsible for the review, conflicting information provided by multiple representatives, and the significant financial hardship that resulted. My complaint is not that Wells Fargo conducted a security review. I understand that financial institutions have an obligation to investigate transactions when appropriate to protect customers and the banking system. My complaint concerns the manner in which Wells Fargo handled the review, failed to communicate with me, repeatedly prevented me from speaking with the department responsible for the decision, and failed to provide accurate or consistent information throughout the process. Background A XXXX payment in the amount of {$1000.00} was sent to my personal Wells Fargo account by an individual who has successfully sent me funds numerous times in the past. When the payment did not become available, I discovered that Wells Fargo had placed the funds under a security review. At no time before or after placing the hold on my funds did Wells Fargo notify me that my payment had been restricted. Unlike previous instances in which Wells Fargo has contacted me by text message or telephone regarding potentially suspicious activity or declined transactions, I received : No text message No telephone call No email No secure message No notification of any kind I only became aware of the issue after attempting to access the funds myself. Because I received no notification, I had no opportunity to make alternative financial arrangements before discovering that the funds were unavailable. Repeated Attempts to Obtain Assistance After discovering the hold, I contacted Wells Fargo seeking information regarding the status of my payment. During multiple calls, I repeatedly requested to speak with the department responsible for placing the security review on my funds or with someone who had the authority to explain the review and advise me whether anything was required from me to complete the process. Instead, I was repeatedly told that representatives : Could not identify the department handling my case. Could not transfer me to that department. Could not provide me with a direct telephone number. Could not explain why my funds had been placed on hold. Could not tell me whether anyone had reviewed my transaction. Could not tell me whether additional information was required from me. I explained multiple times that I was not asking representatives to override the review. I simply wanted the opportunity to communicate with the department responsible for reviewing my transaction so I could determine : Whether my transaction had actually been reviewed. Whether Wells Fargo needed additional information from me. Whether I could verify my identity immediately. Whether there was anything I could do to expedite the review. When I could reasonably expect access to my funds. Despite making these requests repeatedly, I was denied the ability to communicate with the department responsible for the decision affecting my funds. In my opinion, preventing a customer from communicating with the department responsible for restricting access to their money, while simultaneously refusing to provide meaningful information regarding the status of the review, is a serious customer service concern that warrants review. Multiple Transfers and Conflicting Information Instead of receiving answers, I spent several hours being transferred between departments. During XXXX call, after requesting to speak with a supervisor because representatives repeatedly stated they could not assist me, my call was disconnected. After calling back, I explained what had occurred and was transferred to the XXXX Department. The XXXX representative informed me they could not transfer me to the department responsible for the review. My call was then transferred to XXXX XXXX. The XXXX XXXX representative advised me that I had actually been transferred to the wrong fraud department. He submitted an escalation request and specifically advised me that I would receive a telephone call before the end of that same day. Because I relied upon that representation, I waited for the promised call. No one contacted me. When I called Wells Fargo again later that day, I was no longer told I would receive a callback that day. Instead, I was informed that the review would now require XXXX to XXXX hours, directly contradicting the information previously provided. During another call, I was finally informed that the department handling my case was Loss XXXX. This was the first time anyone identified the department responsible for the review. I was then provided with a telephone number for that department. However, by the time I finally received that information, the department had already closed for the day. As a result, after spending several hours attempting to locate the correct department, I was still unable to speak with anyone who could answer my questions. Financial Hardship Because Wells Fargo failed to notify me that my funds had been placed under review, I was left without access to money that I depended upon for basic living expenses. The inability to access these funds affected my ability to purchase food and created concerns regarding transportation to work. Had Wells Fargo simply notified me that the payment had been placed under review, I could have made alternative arrangements before experiencing these hardships. Attempt to File a Complaint with Wells Fargo Following these events, I contacted Wells Fargo 's XXXX XXXX complaint line to file a formal complaint. I spoke with a representative identified as XXXX, who documented my complaint and provided me with the following complaint reference number : Complaint ID : XXXX XXXX advised that my complaint would be forwarded internally. During that conversation, I requested a corporate email address or mailing address so I could submit a formal written complaint directly to Wells Fargo. I was advised that no corporate email address could be provided. When I requested a corporate mailing address, I was initially told one could not be provided. After independently locating what appeared to be Wells Fargo 's corporate office address, I asked whether the following address was correct : Wells Fargo XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX, CA XXXX XXXX advised that he could not confirm whether the address was correct because he worked in a call center. I found it concerning that even while attempting to file a formal complaint, Wells Fargo could not verify where a customer should send written correspondence to the company 's corporate office. Requested Resolution I respectfully request that the CFPB XXXX Wells Fargo 's handling of this matter and require the bank to provide a written response addressing the following : Why I was not notified that my funds had been placed under security review. Why I was repeatedly denied the opportunity to communicate with the department responsible for placing and maintaining the hold on my funds. Why representatives repeatedly refused to transfer me to the department responsible for my case or provide contact information until after the department had closed. Why I received conflicting information regarding callback commitments and review timeframes. Whether Wells Fargo 's policies regarding customer notification and communication were properly followed in this instance. What corrective actions, if any, Wells Fargo intends to implement to improve customer notification, internal communication, and complaint handling. I appreciate the CFPB 's review of this matter and respectfully request that this complaint be forwarded to Wells Fargo for a formal written response. Thank you for your time and consideration. Respectfully, XXXX XXXX

Consumer complaint narrative: Merchant confirmed there was no charge, I was not physically present and I have had my card in my possession the entire time so a charge using my chip was impossible. Heres what could have happened When your bank claims that " XXXX said the chip was used, '' they are referring to a data tag known as " XXXX XXXX '' or XXXX data embedded in the electronic transaction authorization. Under strict Visa Claims Resolution ( VCR ) rules, when a transaction is flagged with this tag, the network systematically blocks the bank from automatically filing an " unauthorized fraud '' dispute because XXXX chips are cryptographically unique and theoretically impossible to clone The " Fallback '' Exploit : Fraudsters clone a card 's magnetic stripe but deliberately damage the fake chip. When they try inserting it at a terminal, it fails multiple times, forcing the terminal to " fall back '' to a stripe swipe. A software glitch at the point-of-sale terminal can mistakenly pass this authorization to XXXX with the " XXXX XXXX '' data tag still attached.Incorrect Billing Descriptor : The charge may not actually be from that specific merchant. It could be from a completely different parent company, a third-party payment processor ( like XXXX, XXXX, or XXXX ), or a fraudster intentionally spoofing the merchant 's name on your bank statement to hide their activity.Authorization Ghosting : It could be a processing glitch where a transaction was aborted mid-way, leaving a " pending '' authorization stuck on your account that the merchant 's accounting software never finalized or integrated into their sales ledger.
